definitions.gloss: many; a large number of; a lot of (attributive modifier)
definitions.explanation: An attributive phrase formed from the noun {多|おお}く (a great many, a lot) plus the particle の. Used before a noun to mean "many of X" or "a large number of X." More written and formal than たくさんの; a standard choice in news, essays, and academic writing.

examples.japanese: {多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{集|あつ}まった。
{多|おお}くの{場合|ばあい}、この{方法|ほうほう}が{有効|ゆうこう}だ。
examples.english: In many cases, this method is effective.

examples.japanese: {多|おお}くの{学生|がくせい}が、{卒業|そつぎょう}{後|ご}も{恩師|おんし}と{連絡|れんらく}を{取|と}り{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: Many students continue to stay in touch with their former teachers even after graduation.

examples.japanese: この{研究|けんきゅう}は、{医療|いりょう}{現場|げんば}における{多|おお}くの{課題|かだい}を{解決|かいけつ}する{手|て}がかりを{与|あた}えてくれた。
examples.english: This research provided clues for solving many of the issues facing the medical field.

notes:
Built from the noun {多|おお}く ("many; a lot" — the nominal form of the i-adjective {多|おお}い) + の. The resulting phrase functions as an attributive modifier, always placed before a noun.

CORE PATTERN:
  {多|おお}くの + noun = "many [noun]" / "a lot of [noun]"

KEY GRAMMATICAL CONTRAST (important!):
{多|おお}い and {多|おお}くの behave differently:
- {多|おお}い is an i-adjective, but it is NOT used attributively before a noun in modern Japanese: *{多|おお}い{人|ひと} is unnatural.
- Instead, use {多|おお}くの{人|ひと} to mean "many people."
- Or use {多|おお}い as a predicate: {人|ひと}が{多|おお}い ("the people are many / there are many people").

So the choice between {多|おお}くの and {多|おお}い depends on the position:
- Attributive (before noun): {多|おお}くの + noun
- Predicate (after noun): noun + が/は + {多|おお}い

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {多|おお}くの{人|ひと}: many people
- {多|おお}くの{場合|ばあい}: in many cases
- {多|おお}くの{時間|じかん}: a lot of time
- {多|おお}くの{問題|もんだい}: many problems
- {多|おお}くの{国|くに}: many countries
- {多|おお}くの{学生|がくせい}: many students
- {多|おお}くの{企業|きぎょう}: many companies

SIMILAR WORDS:
- たくさんの: many, lots of — conversational; used with both countable and uncountable nouns. More frequent in speech.
- {大勢|おおぜい}の: many (only for people; crowds of people)
- {数|かず}{多|おお}くの: numerous (even more emphatic than {多|おお}くの; written)
- {数多|あまた}: many (literary; somewhat archaic)
- いろんな / {様々|さまざま}な: various (emphasizes variety rather than raw count)

REGISTER:
{多|おお}くの is the standard written and semi-formal choice. It appears in newspapers, essays, textbooks, speeches, and business writing. In everyday conversation, たくさんの or simply たくさん is more natural.

WATCH OUT:
Learners who start from the adjective {多|おお}い often try *{多|おお}い{人|ひと} or *{多|おお}い{問題|もんだい}. These are ungrammatical in modern Japanese. Whenever you need to say "many X" as a modifier before a noun, use {多|おお}くの + noun.
